knowledge_point.title: Reducing an Augmented Matrix for a Singular 2x2 System to REF and Solving the Resulting System

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The system corresponding to $M$ is 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y &=3 \\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+2y=3.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=3-2y,$ and the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=3-2y \\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3-2y \\ y\end{bmatrix}=⟨3-2y,\,y⟩,\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

Find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The system corresponding to $M$ is 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y &=-3\\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+2y=-3.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=-2y-3,$ and the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-2y-3\\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix} x  \\ y \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} -2y-3 \\ y \end{bmatrix}=⟨-2y-3,y⟩,\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}3 & -2 & 1 \\ 6 & -4 & 2\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}3 & -2 & 1 \\ 6 & -4 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 6 & -4 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 8 & 16 & -8\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 8 & 16 & -8\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-8){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y &=-1 \\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+2y=-1.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=-1-2y,$ and the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-1-2y \\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-1-2y \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & -1 \\ -5 & -10 & 5\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y &=-1 \\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+2y=-1.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=-1-2y,$ and the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-1-2y \\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-1-2y \\ y\end{bmatrix}\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
